newsitem.title: ITALY: Gemina sharp rise after analysts meeting.
newsitem.headline: Gemina sharp rise after analysts meeting.

text.p: Shares in Italian financial holding group Gemina rose sharply on Tuesday after a meeting on Monday which gave analysts a more favourable valuation for the group.

The group gave a breakdown of how Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) performed in the first half of 1996, after it announced its industrial holdings would be formed into a new holding company called HPI by the end of the year leaving largely its financial interests in the remaining Gemina company.
Gemina shares were up 5.22 percent at 740 lire at 1415 GMT in a firmer Milan bourse.

Brokers Intersim had posted a buy order on the shares after the meeting. Group analyst Gianni Allavena sees a target price of 850/900 lire a share. He said at first the broker was neutral but had changed its mind after the plan to split the company.
Other brokers were also positive with Albertini and Pasfin confirming their buy recommendation.
